request_user:
Fact definition: How and why key design choices in training were made.
Extracted value: The card gives rationales for some design choices. Hybrid attention (local sliding window interleaved with global) gives the speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without losing deep awareness for long-context tasks. Training data includes code to learn programming syntax and patterns, and mathematical text to learn logical reasoning, symbolic representation and to address mathematical queries.
Quotes given as evidence (separated by [...]): This hybrid design delivers the processing speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing the deep awareness required for complex, long-context tasks. [...] Exposing the model to code helps it to learn the syntax and patterns of programming languages, which improves its ability to generate code and understand code-related questions. [...] Training on mathematical text helps the model learn logical reasoning, symbolic representation, and to address mathematical queries.

Grade the extraction:
- "y": the quotes are about this model and support every claim in the value, and the value answers the fact definition.
- "partial": mostly right, but the value adds claims the quotes don't support, drops an important qualifier, or only partly answers the definition.
- "n": wrong, unsupported, about a different model, or does not answer the definition.

answer.reason: The quotes are from this card and support each stated rationale (hybrid attention; code and maths data). However, the value covers only some of the explicit design rationales the card gives. It leaves out PLE (parameter efficiency on device), the encoder-free 12B Unified model (lower latency, single-pass fine-tuning), unified KV/p-RoPE (memory for long context), MoE (fast inference) and the data filtering rationale (safety and reliability). Hybrid attention is also an architecture choice more than a training choice. So it only partly answers the definition.
